parsed.explanation: There is no documented offence for trans presentation, routine border scrutiny, or general facility-access ban. The strongest visitor-facing warning is a 2024 case in which a trans foreign national was placed in a male guarded centre and denied hormones for three months. This is serious, but one case does not establish a recurring policy; NGO intervention secured her release. A separate court ruling found prison authorities had unlawfully denied a trans prisoner hormones and awarded damages, evidence of some effective recourse, though not proof that detention practice is reliably safe. The dossier also documents hostile rhetoric, a violent counter-protest and broader social conservatism, but much of this evidence is dated or not specifically about visitors. Resident-only recognition and rights gaps do not directly determine visitor exposure. The record is incomplete, so silence on other visitor-facing risks is not proof of safety; overall, risk is reduced but meaningfully above low.
